title: Japanese Tuna Mayo Rice Balls
summary: Simple onigiri-style rice balls filled with creamy tuna mayo and a little spring onion. They make a quick, satisfying pescatarian lunch that is easy to pack or eat by hand.

ingredients.name: vegetable stock for cooking the rice

steps: Put the rinsed sushi rice and vegetable stock in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then cover, reduce the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes, until the grains are tender and sticky.
Meanwhile, mix the drained tuna, mayonnaise, soy sauce and sliced spring onion in a bowl until creamy and well combined.
Tip the cooked rice into a wide bowl and let it cool for 5 minutes, until warm enough to handle but still sticky. Sprinkle over the salt and sesame seeds and gently fold through.
Wet your hands with water to stop sticking. Take a handful of rice, flatten it slightly, add a spoonful of tuna mayo to the centre, then cover with more rice and press firmly into a ball or triangle.
Repeat to make 4 rice balls. Serve straight away, or cool completely and pack for lunch the same day.
